objects.description: Execution/context state used while scanning and validating ZIP archives. Tracks configuration flags and cumulative accounting (nesting depth, number of files/archives, total sizes, and cumulative compressed/uncompressed sizes) to enforce anti-zip-bomb limits during parsing and recursion.

Parsed view of a ZIP Local File Header (LFH). Contains decoded fixed fields, pointers into the original buffer for the variable-length file name and extra field, aggregate byte lengths, and a flag indicating ZIP64 usage.
Parsed view of a ZIP Data Descriptor Record (DDR), optionally ZIP64-sized. Holds checksum and sizes that may follow file data when bit 3 (data descriptor) is set.

Parsed view of a ZIP Central Directory Header (CDH). Includes decoded fixed-size fields, pointers to variable-length name/extra/comment within the source buffer, derived attributes (unix_mode, directory), relative LFH offset, and ZIP64 indicator.
Parsed ZIP64 End of Central Directory Record. Holds central directory location/size and counts in 64-bit form plus a pointer to the variable-length extensible data sector.
Parsed ZIP64 End of Central Directory Locator. Points to the ZIP64 EOCDR and records disk information.

Parsed End of Central Directory Record (classic 32-bit). Contains central directory span and a pointer to the optional archive comment. The zip64 flag is set when upgraded by the ZIP64 EOCD structures.

functions.name: pure_zip_crc32
functions.signature: int pure_zip_crc32(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, uint64_t* result)
functions.description: Computes CRC32 over the given buffer using zlib crc32_z and returns it via result. Intended for verifying ZIP entry data integrity.
requirements: buffer must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
size must be <= SIZE_MAX (enforced by assert) and fit into unsigned long for zlib (code asserts compressed_size <= UINT32_MAX equivalently via size check path).
result must be non-NULL and must initially point to a uint64_t set to 0 (asserts *result == 0).
On success returns 0; never returns negative; maps zlib to simple success path.

functions.name: pure_zip_debug_lfh
functions.signature: void pure_zip_debug_lfh(const pure_zip_lfh* header)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of a Local File Header (LFH) to stdout for debugging.
requirements: header must be a valid, fully-decoded pure_zip_lfh pointer with fields and pointer members (file_name/extra_field) valid for their lengths.
Writes to stdout; caller should ensure IO is acceptable.

functions.name: pure_zip_debug_ddr
functions.signature: void pure_zip_debug_ddr(const pure_zip_ddr* header)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of a Data Descriptor Record (DDR) to stdout for debugging.
requirements: header must be a valid, fully-decoded pure_zip_ddr pointer with fields set.
Writes to stdout.

functions.name: pure_zip_debug_cdh
functions.signature: void pure_zip_debug_cdh(const pure_zip_cdh* header)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of a Central Directory Header (CDH) to stdout for debugging, including file name and comment bytes.
requirements: header must be a valid, fully-decoded pure_zip_cdh pointer with file_name/extra_field/file_comment pointers valid for their lengths.
Writes to stdout.

functions.name: pure_zip_debug_eocdl_64
functions.signature: void pure_zip_debug_eocdl_64(const pure_zip_eocdl_64* header)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of the ZIP64 End of Central Directory Locator to stdout.
requirements: header must be a valid, decoded pure_zip_eocdl_64 struct.
Writes to stdout.

functions.name: pure_zip_debug_eocdr_64
functions.signature: void pure_zip_debug_eocdr_64(const pure_zip_eocdr_64* header)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of the ZIP64 End of Central Directory Record to stdout.
requirements: header must be a valid, decoded pure_zip_eocdr_64 struct.
Writes to stdout.

functions.name: pure_zip_debug_eocdr
functions.signature: void pure_zip_debug_eocdr(const pure_zip_eocdr* header)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable dump of the End of Central Directory Record (EOCDR) to stdout, including comment bytes.
requirements: header must be a valid, decoded pure_zip_eocdr with comment pointer valid for comment_length.
Writes to stdout.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_compression_ratio
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_compression_ratio(const uint64_t compressed_size, const uint64_t uncompressed_size)
functions.description: Heuristically evaluates compression ratio risk combining ratio and uncompressed size and returns an error code if it exceeds the configured limit; helps detect ZIP bombs.
requirements: compressed_size and uncompressed_size are raw sizes for either a file or an aggregate; zero compressed_size is allowed and returns 0 to avoid division by zero.
Uses constants PURE_ZIP_COMPRESSION_RATIO_SIZE_MIN and PURE_ZIP_COMPRESSION_RATIO_SCORE_MAX for policy.
Returns 0 if acceptable, or PURE_E_ZIP_BOMB_RATIO on excessive score.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_compression_method
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_compression_method(const uint64_t value)
functions.description: Validates the ZIP compression method field against allowed methods and known unsafe or unsupported values.
requirements: value is a ZIP method ID; 0 (store) and 8 (deflate) are accepted.
value > 999 returns PURE_E_ZIP_COMPRESSION_METHOD_DANGEROUS (CVE-2016-9844 mitigation).
value == 99 returns PURE_E_ZIP_COMPRESSION_METHOD_ENCRYPTED.
Other values return PURE_E_ZIP_COMPRESSION_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED.
Returns 0 only for supported methods.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_compression_method_sizes
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_compression_method_sizes(const uint64_t compression_method, const uint64_t compressed_size, const uint64_t uncompressed_size)
functions.description: Validates the combination of method and sizes: checks method validity, ensures stored entries have equal sizes, and guards against pathological negative ratios (overflow-prone cases).
requirements: Callers provide raw sizes from headers.
If compression_method == 0 (store), then compressed_size must equal uncompressed_size; otherwise returns PURE_E_ZIP_STORED_COMPRESSION_SIZE_MISMATCH.
If uncompressed_size > 0, compressed_size > uncompressed_size, and compressed_size/uncompressed_size >= 2 then returns PURE_E_ZIP_DANGEROUS_NEGATIVE_COMPRESSION_RATIO.
Also returns nonzero if method itself is invalid per pure_zip_verify_compression_method.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_date
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_date(const uint64_t value)
functions.description: Validates an MS-DOS date packed into 16 bits: checks bit width and ensures year (<=2099), month (<=12), day (<=31) are within supported ranges.
requirements: value must fit in 16 bits; otherwise PURE_E_ZIP_DATE_OVERFLOW.
Years after 2099 (relative to 1980 base) are rejected with PURE_E_ZIP_DATE_YEAR_OVERFLOW.
Month > 12 -> PURE_E_ZIP_DATE_MONTH_OVERFLOW; day > 31 -> PURE_E_ZIP_DATE_DAY_OVERFLOW.
Returns 0 if valid.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_directory
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_directory(const pure_zip_cdh* header)
functions.description: Ensures directory entries declare zero compressed and uncompressed sizes; non-directory entries are accepted as-is.
requirements: header->directory must be 0 or 1 (assert).
If header->directory is true, compressed_size and uncompressed_size must both be 0, else returns PURE_E_ZIP_DIRECTORY_COMPRESSED/UNCOMPRESSED.
Returns 0 otherwise.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_disk
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_disk(const uint64_t value)
functions.description: Verifies that the disk number equals 0 (single-disk archives only).
requirements: value must be 0; otherwise returns PURE_E_ZIP_MULTIPLE_DISKS.
Returns 0 if value == 0.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_extra_field
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_extra_field(const uint8_t* extra_field, const uint64_t extra_field_length, const uint8_t* file_name, const uint64_t file_name_length)
functions.description: Validates a ZIP extra field blob: bounds, well-formed TLV chunks, UTF-8 path (0x7075) handling, and detects under/overflow and overlong sizes. Ensures Unicode Path extra (0x7075) content matches the central directory file name exactly.
requirements: extra_field must point to extra_field_length readable bytes.
extra_field_length must be <= PURE_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_MAX; if !=0 it must be >= 4 (else PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_MIN).
Each attribute must fit within extra_field_length; otherwise PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_ATTRIBUTE_OVERFLOW.
For id 0x7075 (Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra), size must be at least 5 (1 version + 4 crc32); version must be 1, else PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_UNICODE_PATH_VERSION.
For id 0x7075, the trailing Unicode path bytes must match file_name exactly in length and content; else PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_UNICODE_PATH_DIFF.

If trailing bytes remain within the 0x0001 block (Zip64 block not parsed here) or any block, nonzero underflow region yields PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_UNDERFLOW_BUFFER_BLEED, zeroed yields PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_UNDERFLOW_ZEROED.
On general loop completion if offset > length returns PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_OVERFLOW.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_file_name
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_file_name(const uint8_t* file_name, const uint64_t file_name_length)
functions.description: Validates a ZIP file name/path against traversal and policy: length limit, no control chars, no drive/relative/.. traversal, component size limits, and prohibits backslashes.
requirements: file_name must point to file_name_length readable bytes; length may be 0.
file_name_length must be <= PURE_PATH_MAX else PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_LENGTH.
Must not contain control characters that mask traversal (checked via pure_path_control_characters) else PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_CONTROL_CHARACTERS.
Must not be drive-based paths -> PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_TRAVERSAL_DRIVE_PATH.
Must not be relative paths -> PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_TRAVERSAL_RELATIVE_PATH.
Must not contain ".." traversal -> PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_TRAVERSAL_DOUBLE_DOTS.
No component overflow -> PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_COMPONENT_OVERFLOW.
All slashes must be forward; any '\' -> PURE_E_ZIP_FILE_NAME_BACKSLASH.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_flags
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_flags(const uint64_t value)
functions.description: Validates ZIP General Purpose Bit Flag field: enforces 16-bit width and rejects unsupported, reserved, or dangerous bits per policy and ISO/IEC 21320-1:2015.
requirements: value must be <= PURE_16_BIT_MAX, else PURE_E_ZIP_FLAG_OVERFLOW.

Rejects bits: 0 (traditional encryption), 4 (enhanced deflate), 5 (compressed patched data), 6 (strong encryption), 7, 8, 9, 10 (unused), 12 (enhanced compression), 13 (masked local headers), 14/15 (reserved). Each returns a specific error code.
Returns 0 if none of the forbidden bits are set.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_string
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_string(const uint8_t* string, const uint64_t string_length, const uint64_t utf8)
functions.description: Validates a general ZIP string blob (file name/comment): size limit and absence of NUL bytes; placeholder for future UTF-8 validation when utf8 is nonzero.
requirements: string must point to string_length readable bytes.
string_length must be <= PURE_ZIP_STRING_MAX; else PURE_E_ZIP_STRING_MAX.
No zero bytes allowed; NUL anywhere -> PURE_E_ZIP_STRING_NULL_BYTE.
If utf8 is nonzero, note that UTF-8 validity is not currently enforced (comment). Returns 0 otherwise.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_symlink
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_symlink(const pure_zip_cdh* cdh, const pure_zip_lfh* lfh, const uint8_t* buffer)
functions.description: If the entry is a Unix symlink, validates it is stored (no compression), and checks the symlink target path for traversal and component policies. Non-symlinks return 0.
requirements: If not a symlink based on cdh->unix_mode, returns 0.
For symlinks: cdh->compression_method must be 0 (store) else PURE_E_ZIP_SYMLINK_COMPRESSED.
cdh->relative_offset must equal lfh->offset (assert).
buffer must contain the entire file; symlink data is at buffer + cdh->relative_offset + lfh->length with length cdh->compressed_size.
Symlink target length must be <= PURE_PATH_MAX else PURE_E_ZIP_SYMLINK_LENGTH.
Target must not contain control characters -> PURE_E_ZIP_SYMLINK_CONTROL_CHARACTERS.
Must not be drive/relative/.. traversal -> respective errors.
No component overflow -> PURE_E_ZIP_SYMLINK_COMPONENT_OVERFLOW.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_unix_mode
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_unix_mode(const uint64_t value)
functions.description: Validates Unix mode bits from external attributes: rejects device, FIFO, socket types and sticky/setgid/setuid permission bits; also ensures it fits 16 bits.
requirements: value must be <= PURE_16_BIT_MAX else PURE_E_ZIP_UNIX_MODE_OVERFLOW.
Rejects BLK -> PURE_E_ZIP_UNIX_MODE_BLOCK_DEVICE; CHR -> PURE_E_ZIP_UNIX_MODE_CHARACTER_DEVICE; FIFO -> PURE_E_ZIP_UNIX_MODE_FIFO; SOCK -> PURE_E_ZIP_UNIX_MODE_SOCKET.
Rejects permissions: sticky (512), setgid (1024), setuid (2048).
Returns 0 if acceptable.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_time
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_time(const uint64_t value)
functions.description: Validates an MS-DOS time packed into 16 bits: hour (<=23), minute (<=59), second (even, <=59), and ensures 16-bit range.
requirements: value must be <= PURE_16_BIT_MAX else PURE_E_ZIP_TIME_OVERFLOW.
If hour > 23 -> PURE_E_ZIP_TIME_HOUR_OVERFLOW; minute > 59 -> PURE_E_ZIP_TIME_MINUTE_OVERFLOW; second (value&31)*2 > 59 -> PURE_E_ZIP_TIME_SECOND_OVERFLOW.
Returns 0 if valid.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_lfh
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_lfh(const pure_zip_lfh* header)
functions.description: Performs semantic validation of a decoded Local File Header: checks lengths, flags, method+sizes, MS-DOS date/time, file name and string rules, and extra field semantics. Ensures ZIP64 indicator is boolean.
requirements: header must be decoded with length/file_name/extra_field pointers valid and sizes consistent (assert that length equals base+name+extra).
General Purpose Bit Flag must pass pure_zip_verify_flags.
Compression method and sizes must pass pure_zip_verify_compression_method_sizes.
Date/time must pass pure_zip_verify_date/time.
File name must pass pure_zip_verify_file_name and pure_zip_verify_string (utf8 follows bit 11).
Extra field must pass pure_zip_verify_extra_field.
header->zip64 must be 0 or 1 (assert).
Returns first nonzero error encountered; 0 on success.

functions.name: pure_zip_verify_cdh
functions.signature: int pure_zip_verify_cdh(const pure_zip_cdh* header)
functions.description: Performs semantic validation of a decoded Central Directory Header: flags, method+sizes, non-ex-nihilo sizes, MS-DOS date/time, file name/comment strings, extra field, single-disk, Unix mode, and directory invariants. Ensures ZIP64 indicator is boolean.
requirements: header must be decoded with length/file_name/extra_field/file_comment pointers valid and sizes consistent (assert length equals base+name+extra+comment).
Flags verified via pure_zip_verify_flags.
Compression method/sizes via pure_zip_verify_compression_method_sizes; also rejects compressed_size==0 with uncompressed_size!=0 (PURE_E_ZIP_EX_NIHILO).
Date/time via pure_zip_verify_date/time.
File name and comment via pure_zip_verify_file_name/pure_zip_verify_string (utf8 per bit 11).
Extra field via pure_zip_verify_extra_field.
Disk must be 0 via pure_zip_verify_disk.
Unix mode via pure_zip_verify_unix_mode; directory invariants via pure_zip_verify_directory.
header->zip64 must be 0 or 1 (assert).

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_eief_64
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_eief_64(const uint8_t* extra_field, const uint64_t length, uint64_t* compressed_size, uint64_t* uncompressed_size, uint64_t* relative_offset, uint64_t* disk, uint8_t* zip64, uint8_t lfh)
functions.description: Parses the Zip64 Extended Information Extra Field (ID 0x0001) within an extra_field blob and upgrades size/offset/disk fields that were maxed out in 32-bit headers. Sets zip64 to 1 if present and valid.
requirements: Callers must initialize *compressed_size, *uncompressed_size, *relative_offset to either actual values or PURE_32_BIT_MAX and *disk to actual or PURE_16_BIT_MAX; at least one must be maxed (assert).
*zip64 must be initialized to 0 (assert). lfh must be 0 or 1 (assert); if lfh==1, exactly uncompressed+compressed (16 bytes) must be present in this block; otherwise PURE_E_ZIP_EIEF_64_LFH.
length must be <= PURE_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_MAX and either 0 or >=4, else PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_MAX/MIN.
The 0x0001 block must not overflow length; otherwise PURE_E_ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_ATTRIBUTE_OVERFLOW.
If any expected field is missing due to short size, returns the corresponding PURE_E_ZIP_EIEF_64_* error.
If extra bytes remain in the 0x0001 block, returns UNDERFLOW_* errors depending on zeroed versus nonzero content.
Returns 0 on success or if no 0x0001 block is found; sets zip64=1 only when 0x0001 is parsed.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_lfh
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_lfh(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, const uint64_t offset, pure_zip_lfh* header)
functions.description: Decodes a Local File Header at the given offset in buffer into header, handling Zip64 size upgrades from its extra field, and verifies it via pure_zip_verify_lfh.
requirements: offset < size (assert).
buffer must contain at least PURE_ZIP_LFH_MIN bytes at offset; else PURE_E_ZIP_LFH_OVERFLOW.
Signature at offset must match PURE_S_ZIP_LFH; else PURE_E_ZIP_LFH_SIGNATURE.
Derived pointers file_name and extra_field must not overflow the buffer; else respective PURE_E_ZIP_LFH_*_OVERFLOW errors.
If either size field is 0xFFFFFFFF, attempts Zip64 decode via pure_zip_decode_eief_64 with lfh=1; errors propagate.
On success, pure_zip_verify_lfh must pass; otherwise its error is returned.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_ddr
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_ddr(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, uint64_t offset, pure_zip_ddr* header)
functions.description: Decodes a Data Descriptor Record at offset, with or without signature, using 32-bit or 64-bit form according to header->zip64. Populates lengths and values and returns 0.
requirements: offset < size (assert).
header->zip64 must be 0 or 1 (assert) prior to call to choose size layout.
There must be at least minimal bytes available: PURE_L_ZIP_DDR followed by the min payload; otherwise PURE_E_ZIP_DDR_OVERFLOW.
If signature present, it is accounted in header->offset/length; otherwise decoding starts immediately at offset.
For zip64 form, payload sizes must follow 4+8+8; for 32-bit form 4+4+4; otherwise overflow errors apply.
Returns 0 on success.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_cdh
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_cdh(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, const uint64_t offset, pure_zip_cdh* header)
functions.description: Decodes a Central Directory Header at offset, sets pointers to variable-length regions, derives unix_mode and directory flag, applies Zip64 extra upgrades as needed, performs critical offset sanity checks, then validates via pure_zip_verify_cdh.
requirements: offset < size (assert).
Must have at least PURE_ZIP_CDH_MIN bytes; else PURE_E_ZIP_CDH_OVERFLOW.
Signature must match PURE_S_ZIP_CDH; else PURE_E_ZIP_CDH_SIGNATURE.
file_name/extra_field/file_comment regions must not overflow; else respective PURE_E_ZIP_CDH_*_OVERFLOW errors.
If version_made indicates UNIX, unix_mode is external_file_attributes >> 16; directory flag is determined by unix_mode, DOS dir attr bit, or trailing '/'.
If any of compressed_size, uncompressed_size, relative_offset, or disk are maxed (FFFFFFFF/FFFF), attempts Zip64 upgrade via pure_zip_decode_eief_64; errors propagate.
relative_offset must be <= size and <= current offset; otherwise PURE_E_ZIP_CDH_RELATIVE_OFFSET_OVERFLOW/OVERLAP.
pure_zip_verify_cdh must pass; otherwise returns its error.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_eocdl_64
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_eocdl_64(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, const uint64_t offset, pure_zip_eocdl_64* header)
functions.description: Decodes a ZIP64 End of Central Directory Locator at offset and performs basic validity checks (single disk, offsets within file).
requirements: offset < size (assert).
Must have PURE_ZIP_EOCDL_64 bytes available; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDL_64_OVERFLOW.
Signature must match; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDL_64_SIGNATURE.
disk must be 0; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDL_64_DISK.
eocdr_64_offset + minimum EOCDR64 size must not overflow past header->offset; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_EOCDL_64_OVERFLOW.
disks must be 0 or 1; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDL_64_DISKS.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, const uint64_t offset, pure_zip_eocdr_64* header)
functions.description: Decodes a ZIP64 End of Central Directory Record at offset, computing the extensible data sector length from the stored size field and capturing a pointer to it.
requirements: offset < size (assert).
Must have at least PURE_ZIP_EOCDR_64_MIN bytes; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_64_OVERFLOW.
Signature must match; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_64_SIGNATURE.
Sets header->length to PURE_ZIP_EOCDR_64_MIN and computes extensible_data_sector_length; caller must ensure buffer contains that many bytes if accessed later.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64_inherit
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64_inherit(pure_zip_eocdr* a, const pure_zip_eocdr_64* b)
functions.description: Copies values from a decoded ZIP64 EOCDR into a classic EOCDR where the classic fields were maxed out. Verifies all shared values match after inheritance.
requirements: a and b must be previously decoded EOCDR/EOCDR64 structures.
Only fields in a that are maxed are overwritten; mismatches between a and b after inheritance return specific PURE_E_ZIP_DIFF_EOCDR_* errors.
Returns 0 on success.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64_upgrade
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64_upgrade(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, pure_zip_eocdr* header)
functions.description: Attempts to upgrade a decoded classic EOCDR to ZIP64 by locating the preceding EOCDL64 and EOCDR64, validating layout/zero-fill between structures, and inheriting fields. On success sets header->zip64=1 and adjusts header->offset/length.
requirements: header must already hold a decoded classic EOCDR with comment region accounted in length.
If all fields in header are not maxed (none require upgrade), returns 0 without changes.
header->offset must be >= PURE_ZIP_EOCDL_64; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDL_64_NEGATIVE_OFFSET.
decode of EOCDL64 at header->offset - PURE_ZIP_EOCDL_64 must succeed; PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDL_64_SIGNATURE is treated as no-zip64 and returns 0.
EOCDR64 must be at eocdl_64.eocdr_64_offset; errors propagate from decode.
There must be no overlap/underflow/garbage between EOCDR64 and EOCDL64; otherwise returns PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_EOCDL_64_OVERFLOW/UNDERFLOW_*.
Inherits via pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64_inherit; errors propagate.
On success sets zip64=1, adjusts offset and length to include EOCDR64+EOCDL64.

functions.name: pure_zip_decode_eocdr
functions.signature: int pure_zip_decode_eocdr(const uint8_t* buffer, const uint64_t size, const uint64_t offset, pure_zip_eocdr* header)
functions.description: Decodes the classic End of Central Directory Record at offset; sets comment pointer; may upgrade to ZIP64 by invoking pure_zip_decode_eocdr_64_upgrade; then validates central directory bounds, records counts, and comment string and ensures no appended data remains.
requirements: offset < size (assert).
Must have at least PURE_ZIP_EOCDR_MIN bytes; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_OVERFLOW.
Signature must match; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_SIGNATURE.
Comment region must not overflow; else PURE_E_ZIP_EOCDR_COMMENT_OVERFLOW.
If upgraded to ZIP64, header->offset/length will be adjusted; otherwise they remain as classic EOCDR.
cd_size must be >= cd_records * PURE_ZIP_CDH_MIN, and nonzero size implies nonzero records; otherwise SIZE_OVERFLOW/SIZE_UNDERFLOW errors.
cd_offset + cd_size must not overflow past header->offset; else PURE_E_ZIP_CD_EOCDR_OVERFLOW.
disk and cd_disk must be 0 (single disk) and cd_disk_records == cd_records; else MULTIPLE_DISKS or EOCDR_RECORDS.
Comment must pass pure_zip_verify_string with utf8=0 (CP437).
There must be no data after the EOCDR(+ZIP64 structures); trailing zeroes/nonzeroes cause PURE_E_ZIP_APPENDED_DATA_*.

functions.name: pure_zip_diff_cld
functions.signature: int pure_zip_diff_cld(const uint64_t cdh_value, const uint64_t lfh_value, const pure_zip_lfh* lfh)
functions.description: Compares a value in CDH with the corresponding value in LFH, allowing LFH zero when bit 3 indicates Data Descriptor usage. Returns 0 if consistent, 1 if different.
requirements: lfh must be the decoded LFH associated with the CDH field being compared.
If lfh->general_purpose_bit_flag has bit 3 set and lfh_value==0, considered matching; otherwise exact equality is required.
Returns 0 for match, 1 for mismatch.

functions.name: pure_zip_diff_cdh_ddr
functions.signature: int pure_zip_diff_cdh_ddr(const pure_zip_cdh* cdh, const pure_zip_ddr* ddr)
functions.description: Compares DDR fields (crc32, compressed_size, uncompressed_size) against CDH values; returns specific errors on mismatch.
requirements: cdh and ddr must be decoded for the same file entry.
Returns PURE_E_ZIP_DIFF_DDR_* errors on mismatch; 0 if all match.

functions.name: pure_zip_diff_cdh_lfh
functions.signature: int pure_zip_diff_cdh_lfh(const pure_zip_cdh* cdh, const pure_zip_lfh* lfh)
functions.description: Compares key LFH fields against CDH (flags, method, time/date, crc/size values accounting for DDR, and file name length/content). Returns specific error codes on differences.
requirements: cdh and lfh must be decoded for the same file entry.
Accepts LFH zeroes for crc/size if DDR is indicated (bit 3) via pure_zip_diff_cld; otherwise exact equality required.
Compares file_name_length and byte-for-byte content (assumes prior overflow checks).
Returns 0 if consistent, else specific PURE_E_ZIP_DIFF_LFH_*.

functions.name: pure_zip_diff_ddr_lfh

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces small, valid ZIP-like byte buffers tailored to exercise
# the provided fuzzer stubs. It focuses on assembling coherent structures:
# - EOCDR (classic) possibly with matching Central Directory (CDH) and a single file
# - Matching Local File Header (LFH) and optional Data Descriptor (DDR)
# - A few variants: stored vs deflate method, DDR present vs absent, Unicode Path extra field
# The buffers are valid or near-valid ZIPs so that decode/verify paths can proceed
# beyond signature checks. Sizes are kept small (<4096 bytes).

# ZIP signatures
S_LFH = 0x04034b50
S_CDH = 0x02014b50
S_EOCDR = 0x06054b50
S_DDR = 0x08074b50  # optional signature for data descriptor

# Helpers

def u16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', v & 0xFFFF)

def u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def u64(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

# Simple CRC32 implementation via binascii (standard library)
import binascii

def crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    return binascii.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF

# Build an Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra Field (0x7075) matching file_name
# Layout: [0x75,0x70] [size=1+4+len(name)] [version=1] [crc32(name)] [name bytes]

def make_unicode_path_extra(name_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    name_crc = crc32(name_bytes)
    payload = bytes([1]) + u32(name_crc) + name_bytes
    return u16(0x7075) + u16(len(payload)) + payload

# Build minimal extra field (optionally include Unicode path block)

def build_extra(include_unicode: bool, name_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    extras = []
    if include_unicode:
        extras.append(make_unicode_path_extra(name_bytes))
    # Add a benign padding TLV to exercise parser loop: id 0x5455 (UT) with size 0
    # A zero-size attribute is valid and quickly skipped.
    extras.append(u16(0x5455) + u16(0))
    return b''.join(extras)

# Build a stored (method 0) entry with tiny content

def build_stored_entry(file_name: str, content: bytes, add_ddr: bool, add_unicode_extra: bool) -> bytes:
    name_b = file_name.encode('utf-8')
    extra = build_extra(add_unicode_extra, name_b)
    gpbf = 0
    if add_ddr:
        gpbf |= 1 << 3  # bit 3 indicates data descriptor
    method = 0  # store
    mtime = 0x4000  # 2:00:00
    mdate = 0x21 << 9 | 1 << 5 | 1  # 2001-01-01 approx (DOS date)

    uncompressed = content
    csize = len(uncompressed)
    usize = len(uncompressed)
    crc = crc32(uncompressed)

    # If DDR is used, LFH crc/size fields set to 0 per spec when bit 3 set
    l_crc = 0 if add_ddr else crc
    l_csize = 0 if add_ddr else csize
    l_usize = 0 if add_ddr else usize

    lfh = b''.join([
        u32(S_LFH),
        u16(20),               # version needed
        u16(gpbf),
        u16(method),
        u16(mtime),
        u16(mdate),
        u32(l_crc),
        u32(l_csize),
        u32(l_usize),
        u16(len(name_b)),
        u16(len(extra)),
        name_b,
        extra,
    ])

    data = uncompressed  # stored

    ddr = b''
    if add_ddr:
        # Use signature form of DDR to improve detectability
        ddr = b''.join([
            u32(S_DDR),
            u32(crc),
            u32(csize),
            u32(usize),
        ])

    # Central Directory Header referencing this LFH
    # external attributes: regular file 0100644 shifted into top 16 bits
    unix_mode = 0o100644
    ext_attr = unix_mode << 16
    relative_offset = 0  # LFH at start

    cdh_extra = build_extra(add_unicode_extra, name_b)
    cdh = b''.join([
        u32(S_CDH),
        u16(20),            # version made by
        u16(20),            # version needed
        u16(gpbf),
        u16(method),
        u16(mtime),
        u16(mdate),
        u32(crc),
        u32(csize),
        u32(usize),
        u16(len(name_b)),
        u16(len(cdh_extra)),
        u16(0),             # file comment length
        u16(0),             # disk number start
        u16(0),             # internal attrs
        u32(ext_attr),
        u32(relative_offset),
        name_b,
        cdh_extra,
        # no file comment
    ])

    # EOCDR for single-entry archive
    cd_offset = len(lfh) + len(data) + len(ddr)
    cd_size = len(cdh)
    eocdr = b''.join([
        u32(S_EOCDR),
        u16(0),  # disk
        u16(0),  # cd_disk
        u16(1),  # cd_disk_records
        u16(1),  # cd_records
        u32(cd_size),
        u32(cd_offset),
        u16(0),  # comment length
    ])

    return lfh + data + ddr + cdh + eocdr

# Build a deflate entry with an empty deflate stream (valid 2-byte empty block)
# This exercises inflate paths without heavy data. For DEFLATE, sizes can be zero only with
# the special empty stream; we set sizes to 0 to exercise checks that allow 2-byte empty stream.

def build_deflate_empty_entry(file_name: str, add_ddr: bool, add_unicode_extra: bool) -> bytes:
    name_b = file_name.encode('utf-8')
    extra = build_extra(add_unicode_extra, name_b)
    gpbf = 0
    if add_ddr:
        gpbf |= 1 << 3
    method = 8  # deflate
    mtime = 0x0000
    mdate = 0x0021  # minimal valid date

    # 2-byte empty raw deflate stream is not universally standard, but many parsers
    # accept a minimal empty block sequence of 2 or 3 bytes. We'll use a known valid
    # empty raw deflate block: 0x03 0x00 (BFINAL=1, BTYPE=00, LEN=0, NLEN=0) actually needs 5 bytes.
    # To keep it tiny yet valid, use a single empty stored block header with LEN=0: 0x01 00 FF FF.
    # However, raw deflate requires at least this 5-byte header if ending properly. We'll use 5 bytes.
    compressed = bytes([0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF])
    uncompressed = b''
    csize = len(compressed)
    usize = len(uncompressed)
    crc = crc32(uncompressed)

    l_crc = 0 if add_ddr else crc
    l_csize = 0 if add_ddr else csize
    l_usize = 0 if add_ddr else usize

    lfh = b''.join([
        u32(S_LFH),
        u16(20),
        u16(gpbf),
        u16(method),
        u16(mtime),
        u16(mdate),
        u32(l_crc),
        u32(l_csize),
        u32(l_usize),
        u16(len(name_b)),
        u16(len(extra)),
        name_b,
        extra,
    ])

    data = compressed

    ddr = b''
    if add_ddr:
        ddr = b''.join([
            u32(S_DDR),
            u32(crc),
            u32(csize),
            u32(usize),
        ])

    unix_mode = 0o100644
    ext_attr = unix_mode << 16
    relative_offset = 0

    cdh_extra = build_extra(add_unicode_extra, name_b)
    cdh = b''.join([
        u32(S_CDH),
        u16(20),
        u16(20),
        u16(gpbf),
        u16(method),
        u16(mtime),
        u16(mdate),
        u32(crc),
        u32(csize),
        u32(usize),
        u16(len(name_b)),
        u16(len(cdh_extra)),
        u16(0),
        u16(0),
        u16(0),
        u32(ext_attr),
        u32(relative_offset),
        name_b,
        cdh_extra,
    ])

    cd_offset = len(lfh) + len(data) + len(ddr)
    cd_size = len(cdh)
    eocdr = b''.join([
        u32(S_EOCDR),
        u16(0),
        u16(0),
        u16(1),
        u16(1),
        u32(cd_size),
        u32(cd_offset),
        u16(0),
    ])

    return lfh + data + ddr + cdh + eocdr

# A minimal classic EOCDR-only buffer (empty archive) to drive locate_eocdr/first_lfh paths

def build_empty_archive() -> bytes:
    # EOCDR with zero records and cd_size=0, cd_offset=0, no comment
    eocdr = b''.join([
        u32(S_EOCDR),
        u16(0), u16(0),
        u16(0), u16(0),
        u32(0), u32(0),
        u16(0),
    ])
    return eocdr

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a variant
    variant = rnd.choice([
        'stored_no_ddr',
        'stored_ddr',
        'deflate_empty_no_ddr',
        'deflate_empty_ddr',
        'empty_archive',
    ])

    # File name variants to exercise file name validation and UTF-8 flag behavior (bit 11 not set here, but names are safe)
    names = [
        'a.txt',
        'path/to/file',
        'readme.md',
        'dir/inner/test',
        'unicodé',
    ]
    file_name = rnd.choice(names)

    # Content for stored entries
    contents = [
        b'',
        b'hello',
        b'ZIP test data',
        bytes([i % 256 for i in range(32)]),
    ]
    content = rnd.choice(contents)

    add_unicode_extra = rnd.choice([True, False])

    if variant == 'empty_archive':
        return build_empty_archive()
    elif variant == 'stored_no_ddr':
        buf = build_stored_entry(file_name, content, add_ddr=False, add_unicode_extra=add_unicode_extra)
    elif variant == 'stored_ddr':
        buf = build_stored_entry(file_name, content, add_ddr=True, add_unicode_extra=add_unicode_extra)
    elif variant == 'deflate_empty_no_ddr':
        buf = build_deflate_empty_entry(file_name, add_ddr=False, add_unicode_extra=add_unicode_extra)
    elif variant == 'deflate_empty_ddr':
        buf = build_deflate_empty_entry(file_name, add_ddr=True, add_unicode_extra=add_unicode_extra)
    else:
        buf = build_empty_archive()

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# ZIP Extra Field generator focused on producing valid TLV sequences with
# interesting combinations for:
# - pure_zip_verify_extra_field(extra_field, extra_field_length, file_name,...)
# - pure_zip_decode_eief_64(extra_field, length, ...)
#
# We emit buffers that are valid concatenations of [id(2)][size(2)][data],
# stressing especially:
# - 0x0001 Zip64 Extended Information blocks with different field subsets
#   and valid sizes, including LFH-specific exact 16-byte data (ucsz+csz).
# - 0x7075 Unicode Path blocks with version=1, crc32 placeholder, and a
#   path that can match or intentionally differ from a companion filename
#   depending on seed path; for the verify_extra_field stub, the harness
#   passes a separate file_name buffer, so our content should often match
#   to be considered valid.
# - Benign unknown tags to exercise TLV traversal.
# We keep sizes small (<= 64 bytes) as the stubs cap input length.

# Helper to write little-endian 16/32/64 integers

def u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return (x & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(2, 'little')

def u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return (x & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little')

def u64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return (x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(8, 'little')

# Build specific extra field blocks

def build_zip64_block(fields: List[str], values: dict) -> bytes:
    # fields order must be: uncompressed_size, compressed_size, relative_offset, disk
    # Only include those listed in fields
    payload = b""
    if 'uncompressed_size' in fields:
        payload += u64(values.get('uncompressed_size', 0))
    if 'compressed_size' in fields:
        payload += u64(values.get('compressed_size', 0))
    if 'relative_offset' in fields:
        payload += u64(values.get('relative_offset', 0))
    if 'disk' in fields:
        payload += u32(values.get('disk', 0))
    return u16(0x0001) + u16(len(payload)) + payload


def build_unicode_path_block(path_bytes: bytes, version: int = 1, crc32_val: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra (0x7075): [ver(1)][crc32(4)][utf8 path]
    payload = bytes([version & 0xFF]) + u32(crc32_val) + path_bytes
    return u16(0x7075) + u16(len(payload)) + payload


def build_unknown_block(tag: int, data_len: int, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    data = bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(data_len))
    return u16(tag & 0xFFFF) + u16(len(data)) + data

# Generate a safe, policy-conformant filename/path for 0x7075 matching

def make_valid_path(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Constraints from verify_file_name/string:
    # - No NULs
    # - No backslashes
    # - No control chars
    # - No leading ./, ../, drive specs, or .. components
    # Keep it short and simple: components of [a-z0-9_-]
    comp_count = rnd.randint(1, 3)
    comps = []
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"
    for _ in range(comp_count):
        L = rnd.randint(1, 10)
        comp = bytes(alphabet[rnd.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(L))
        comps.append(comp)
    # Optionally mark as directory with trailing slash for CDH side, but here we just need name bytes
    path = b"/".join(comps)
    # Avoid trailing slash; Unicode Path compares exact bytes to file_name
    return path


def build_extra_field_bundle(rnd: random.Random, want_lfh_zip64_16: bool, filename_for_7075: bytes) -> bytes:
    blocks: List[bytes] = []

    # Randomly include a Zip64 block
    include_zip64 = rnd.random() < 0.8  # often include, exercises decode_eief_64
    if include_zip64:
        # Choose which fields to include; for LFH strictness path, include exactly ucsz+csz
        if want_lfh_zip64_16:
            fields = ['uncompressed_size', 'compressed_size']
        else:
            # Random subset but non-empty
            all_fields = ['uncompressed_size', 'compressed_size', 'relative_offset', 'disk']
            rnd.shuffle(all_fields)
            k = rnd.randint(1, len(all_fields))
            fields = all_fields[:k]
        vals = {
            'uncompressed_size': rnd.randrange(0, 1 << 20),

    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):

                        blocks[i] = new_block

# Generator for valid ZIP internal path strings per constraints:
# - Length <= 128 (fuzzer truncates); also keep within typical limits
# - Forward slashes only, no backslashes
# - No control characters (use visible ASCII)
# - No drive letters (no patterns like "C:" at start)
# - No relative prefixes: no leading "./" or "../"
# - No ".." path components anywhere
# - No empty component overflows; allow empty string as valid
# - Prefer UTF-8 friendly ASCII subset without NULs
# - Aim to cover directories (trailing '/'), files with extensions, nested paths, hidden names, long components, edge characters like spaces/tilde/plus

VISIBLE_ASCII = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7F))
# Exclude forbidden characters: backslash and colon (to avoid drive paths), and NUL (not in visible anyway)
ALLOWED_CHARS = ''.join(ch for ch in VISIBLE_ASCII if ch not in {'\\', ':'})
# Further restrict component characters to avoid accidental relative components: we'll construct components explicitly
SAFE_COMPONENT_CHARS = ''.join(ch for ch in ALLOWED_CHARS if ch not in {'/'})

EXTS = [
    'txt', 'md', 'bin', 'dat', 'json', 'xml', 'csv', 'png', 'jpg', 'gif', 'webp', 'pdf',
    'zip', 'tar', 'xz', '7z', 'exe', 'dll', 'so', 'dylib'
]

COMP_PREFIXES = ['', 'sub', 'dir', 'folder', 'data', 'res', 'img', 'doc', 'tmp', 'var', 'etc', 'usr', '~user']
COMP_MIDDLES = ['', 'file', 'name', 'part', 'chunk', 'block', 'node', 'asset', 'payload']
COMP_SUFFIXES = ['', '1', '2', 'A', 'B', '-', '_', '+']

SPECIAL_COMPONENTS = [
    # Hidden files and typical names
    '.hidden', '.gitignore', '.env', 'Makefile', 'README', 'LICENSE', 'CHANGELOG',
    # Longish names
    'long_component_name_with_mixed-CHARS_0123456789',
    # Space-containing
    'with space',
    # Non-trivial punctuation (still safe)
    'name~tilde', 'plus+sign', 'equals=sign', 'comma,sep', 'semi;colon', 'at@sign'
]

def rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    # Avoid "." or ".." specifically to satisfy no-traversal rule
    # Sometimes pick from curated components; otherwise synthesize
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        comp = rng.choice(SPECIAL_COMPONENTS)
    else:
        # Construct from prefix/middle/suffix and random tail
        base = rng.choice(COMP_PREFIXES) + rng.choice(COMP_MIDDLES) + rng.choice(COMP_SUFFIXES)
        if base == '':
            base = 'f'
        tail_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, min_len - len(base))) if min_len > len(base) else 0
        tail_len = max(tail_len, rng.randint(0, max(0, max_len - len(base))))
        extra = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_COMPONENT_CHARS) for _ in range(tail_len))
        comp = base + extra
    # Ensure not reserved traversal components
    if comp in {'.', '..'}:
        comp = 'dot' if comp == '.' else 'parent'
    # Strip leading/trailing spaces only occasionally keep (spaces are allowed, but avoid empty after strip)
    if comp.strip() == '':
        comp = 'space'
    return comp

def maybe_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        return '.' + rng.choice(EXTS)
    return ''

def make_directory_path(rng: random.Random, max_total: int) -> str:
    # Build 1-6 components directory path ending with '/'
    n = rng.randint(1, 6)
    comps: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        comp = rand_component(rng)
        comps.append(comp)
    path = '/'.join(comps)
    if not path.endswith('/'):
        path += '/'
    # Ensure within max_total
    if len(path) > max_total:
        path = path[:max_total]
        if not path.endswith('/'):
            # ensure directory semantics
            if len(path) < max_total:
                path = path.rstrip('/') + '/'
            else:
                # replace last char with '/'
                path = path[:-1] + '/'
    return path

def make_file_path(rng: random.Random, max_total: int) -> str:
    # Build depth 0-6; depth 0 means just filename
    depth = rng.randint(0, 6)
    comps: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        comp = rand_component(rng)
        comps.append(comp)
    # filename
    base = rand_component(rng)
    # Occasionally ensure not directory-like
    if base.endswith('/'):
        base = base.rstrip('/') or 'file'
    # add extension
    ext = maybe_extension(rng)
    name = base + ext
    comps.append(name)
    path = '/'.join(comps)
    if len(path) > max_total:
        # Trim conservatively but avoid truncating into a leading './' or '..'
        path = path[:max_total]
        # avoid trailing '/' on files
        path = path.rstrip('/')
        if path == '' or path in {'.', '..'}:
            path = 'file' + maybe_extension(rng)
    return path

def make_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Curated set of valid edge paths
    cases = [
        '',  # empty allowed in some contexts
        'a',
        '0',
        'folder/',
        'folder/sub/',
        'folder/file',
        'folder/file.txt',
        'a/b/c/d/e/f.txt',
        'path/with space/and/mixed-chars_123/file.name',

        'etc/nginx/nginx.conf',
        'verylongcomponentname' * 3 + '/file',
    ]

    filtered = []

        if '\\' in p:
            continue
        if any(comp == '..' for comp in p.split('/') if comp):
            continue
        filtered.append(p)
    rng.shuffle(filtered)
    return filtered

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide type of path to produce
    kind = rng.random()
    max_len = rng.randint(0, 128)

    candidates: List[str] = []
    # Add some curated edge cases
    candidates.extend(make_edge_cases(rng))

    # Synthesize a few random candidates
    for _ in range(10):
        if kind < 0.3:
            p = make_directory_path(rng, max_len)

        # Forward slashes are fine; allow empty string
        valid.append(p)

    # Ensure final length bound
    if len(chosen) > 128:
        chosen = chosen[:128]

# Generator for a "binary string without NULs" for pure_zip_verify_string fuzz stub
# Constraints to honor:
# - No NUL (0x00) bytes in the string payload
# - Length reasonably small (the stub truncates to 128)
# - Cover interesting edge cases for ZIP name/comment validation: control-byte avoidance,
#   mixture of ASCII, CP437-like extended bytes, UTF-8-looking sequences, slashes, dots, etc.

_ASCII_PRINTABLE = [i for i in range(0x20, 0x7F) if i != 0]  # 0x20-0x7E
# CP437-ish high bytes excluding 0x00
_HIGH_BYTES = [i for i in range(0x80, 0x100)]
# Safe path characters (forward slash allowed, backslash not included here; no NUL)
_SAFE_PATH_CHARS = (
    list(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz") +
    list(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ") +
    list(b"0123456789") +
    list(b"-_. /")
)

# Some prebuilt interesting chunks with no NULs
_PRESETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"readme.txt",
    b"docs/manual.pdf",
    b"dir/subdir/file.bin",
    b".hidden/file",
    b"a" * 64,
    b"component" * 12,  # long component to approach component limits
    b"unicode-",
    # Valid 2-byte UTF-8 sequences (no NUL bytes)
    "caf\xc3\xa9".encode("latin1"),  # cafa9
    b"emoji-\xF0\x9F\x98\x80",       # 😀 in UTF-8
    b"space in name/with/slashes",
    b"no-backslash-allowed",
    b"trailing-slash/",
    b"dots.in.name.and.path",
    b"multiple/levels/of/dirs/file.dat",
    b"CP437-\x82\x83\x84\x85\x86",  # some high bytes
]

def _rand_bytes_no_nul(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of ASCII printable and high bytes, excluding NUL
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        kind = rng.random()
        if kind < 0.6:
            out.append(rng.choice(_ASCII_PRINTABLE))
        else:
            out.append(rng.choice(_HIGH_BYTES))
    return bytes(out)

def _rand_path_like(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a path-like string: components separated by '/'
    components = []
    total = 0
    # choose 1-6 components
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)):
        comp_len = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(20, max_len - total - 1)))
        comp = bytearray()
        for _j in range(comp_len):
            comp.append(rng.choice(_SAFE_PATH_CHARS))
        components.append(bytes(comp))
        total += comp_len + 1
        if total >= max_len:
            break
    s = b"/".join(components)
    return s[:max_len]

def _inject_utf8_sequences(rng: random.Random, base: bytearray) -> None:
    # Insert some valid-looking multi-byte UTF-8 sequences that avoid NULs
    sequences = [
        b"\xC2\xA9",           # ©
        b"\xC3\xA9",           # é
        b"\xE2\x82\xAC",       # €
        b"\xF0\x9F\x98\x80",   # 😀
    ]
    if len(base) == 0:
        return
    count = max(1, len(base) // 16)
    for _ in range(count):
        seq = rng.choice(sequences)
        pos = rng.randrange(0, len(base))
        # splice: insert sequence at pos, ensuring max length later
        base[pos:pos] = seq
        if len(base) > 128:
            del base[128:]
            break

def _make_candidate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        # Use a preset
        s = bytearray(rng.choice(_PRESETS))
        # maybe duplicate/extend a bit
        if rng.random() < 0.4 and len(s) < 100:
            s.extend(b"-" + s)
        return bytes(s[:128])
    elif choice < 0.55:
        # Path-like
        s = bytearray(_rand_path_like(rng, rng.randint(8, 128)))
        # optionally inject UTF-8-looking sequences
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            _inject_utf8_sequences(rng, s)
        return bytes(s[:128])
    else:
        # Mixed random without NULs
        length = rng.randint(1, 128)
        s = bytearray(_rand_bytes_no_nul(rng, length))
        # sprinkle some special but non-NUL ASCII that are allowed for names/comments
        specials = b"-_.+/@#()[]{}$^&=,;!~%+"
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)):
            if len(s) == 0:
                break
            pos = rng.randrange(0, len(s))
            s[pos] = rng.choice(list(specials))
        # maybe inject UTF-8 sequences
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            _inject_utf8_sequences(rng, s)
        return bytes(s[:128])

def _ensure_no_nul(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if 0 in data:
        # Replace any accidental NULs with 'A'
        return data.replace(b"\x00", b"A")
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build multiple candidates and choose one to add variety while deterministic per seed
    candidates: List[bytes] = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        candidates.append(_make_candidate(rng))
    # Join candidates with '/' to create a realistic path/comment blend, capped at 128 bytes
    sep = b"/" if rng.random() < 0.6 else b" "
    out = sep.join(candidates)
    if len(out) == 0:
        out = b"file"
    if len(out) > 128:
        out = out[:128]
    out = _ensure_no_nul(out)
    return out

# We need to generate valid raw DEFLATE streams (no zlib/gzip wrapper) that are
# interesting for pure_zip_inflate_raw. The fuzzer stub:
# - Calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for the compressed bytes and truncates to 256 bytes.
# - Picks an uncompressed_size from {0 or 1..1024}.
# - Invokes pure_zip_inflate_raw(compressed, compressed_size, outbuf, uncompressed_size).
# Our generate(seed) should return bytes that become FUZZ_PARAM_STR content.
# Strategy:
# - Produce several families of raw deflate payloads:
#   1) Empty raw stream that decodes to empty output (BFINAL=1 with empty stored block).
#   2) Stored (uncompressed) blocks producing exact lengths across various sizes.
#   3) Fixed Huffman with short literal sequences.
#   4) Dynamic Huffman blocks encoding small patterns, runs, and length/distance backrefs.
#   5) Edge cases: multiple concatenated blocks, end block early, max length codes within small output.
# - We tailor the uncompressed output length to small sizes (<= 512) to keep compressed <= 256.
# - We randomly choose one recipe and synthesize a valid raw deflate stream for it.
# - Keep total size <= 256 and overall buffer <= 4096 (fuzzer truncates to 256 anyway).
# - Do not use wrappers: use zlib.DEFLATED with raw (-15) where we leverage zlib to build a valid stream
#   by compressing chosen plaintext, then post-process if we want multiple blocks (we can concatenate by
#   compressing segments separately and concatenating raw streams). Note: zlib with wbits=-15 yields raw.
#
# We ensure many outputs have exact decompress size that commonly falls into 1..1024.

# Helper: raw deflate compressor

def deflate_raw(data: bytes, level: int = 6, strategy: int = zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY) -> bytes:
    c = zlib.compressobj(level=level, method=zlib.DEFLATED, wbits=-15, memLevel=9, strategy=strategy)
    out = c.compress(data) + c.flush()
    return out

# Build a stored (uncompressed) block manually for small payloads.
# Stored block format in raw deflate:
# - Align to next byte boundary (we assume start already byte-aligned). We'll construct from scratch so aligned.
# - Header: 3 bits: BFINAL (1 bit), BTYPE=00 (2 bits). We pack into little-endian bit order within each byte.
# - Then 16-bit LEN, 16-bit NLEN (one's complement), little-endian.
# - Then LEN bytes of data.
# We'll only build a single, byte-aligned stored block stream.

def deflate_raw_stored_block(payload: bytes, final: bool = True) -> bytes:
    # Build header byte with bits: least-significant bits first in stream
    # For byte-aligned start, the first byte's bit0 is BFINAL, bit1-2 are BTYPE.
    bfinal = 1 if final else 0
    btype = 0  # stored
    first_byte = (bfinal | (btype << 1)) & 0x07
    # LEN and NLEN
    ln = len(payload)
    if ln > 0xFFFF:
        # Split into multiple stored blocks if needed; here we keep <= 64k per block
        parts = []
        offset = 0
        remain = ln
        # First block: not final
        while remain > 0:
            chunk = payload[offset:offset + min(0xFFFF, remain)]
            final_flag = (offset + len(chunk) == ln)
            parts.append(deflate_raw_stored_block(chunk, final=final_flag))
            offset += len(chunk)
            remain -= len(chunk)
        return b"".join(parts)
    nlen = (~ln) & 0xFFFF
    header = bytes([first_byte])
    body = struct.pack('<HH', ln, nlen) + payload
    return header + body

# Build a fixed-Huffman block by leveraging zlib raw compression with strategy FILTERED or HUFFMAN_ONLY.
# zlib may choose dynamic anyway; this is acceptable for validity. We'll vary strategies and levels.

# Create outputs designed to be interesting: ascii text, repetitive, binary, and short patterns.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"hello world\n",
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n",
    b"ZIP\n",
    b"DEF LATE RAW\n",
    b"A" * 64 + b"\n",
]

BINARY_PATTERNS = [
    bytes(range(32)),
    bytes([0x00]) * 128,
    bytes([0xFF]) * 128,
    (b"ABCD" * 32),
]

def make_concatenated_blocks(chunks: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate multiple raw deflate streams to form multiple blocks; valid per zlib inflate.
    return b"".join(deflate_raw(c, level=3) for c in chunks)

def gen_empty_stream() -> bytes:
    # Empty stored block with BFINAL=1, LEN=0, NLEN=0
    return deflate_raw_stored_block(b"", final=True)

def gen_stored_of_length(n: int) -> bytes:
    payload = bytes((i % 251) for i in range(n))
    return deflate_raw_stored_block(payload, final=True)

def gen_text_block(data: bytes, level: int, strategy: int) -> bytes:
    return deflate_raw(data, level=level, strategy=strategy)

def gen_backref_runs(ch: int, total: int) -> bytes:
    # Create data that benefits from LZ back-references: long repeats
    return bytes([ch]) * total

def gen_mixed_payload(rnd: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    remaining = target_len
    while remaining > 0:
        choice = rnd.randint(0, 3)
        take = min(remaining, rnd.randint(1, max(1, min(64, remaining))))
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(bytes([rnd.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(take)]))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(bytes([rnd.choice([0x00, 0x20, 0x41, 0x61, 0xFF])]) * take)
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append((b"./../" * ((take + 3)//4))[:take])
        else:
            parts.append((b"abcde" * ((take + 4)//5))[:take])
        remaining -= take
    return b"".join(parts)

def clamp256(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b if len(b) <= 256 else b[:256]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target uncompressed length to make stream more likely to match fuzzer output buffer size.
    # The fuzzer picks 0 or 1..1024; we aim for common small sizes 0..512.
    target_lengths = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 255, 256, 300, 512]
    target_len = rnd.choice(target_lengths)

    variant = rnd.randint(0, 7)

    if target_len == 0:
        # Empty stream variant choices
        if variant % 2 == 0:
            out = gen_empty_stream()
        else:
            # Valid raw deflate for empty payload via zlib
            out = deflate_raw(b"", level=1)
        return clamp256(out)

    # Non-empty cases
    if variant == 0:
        # Stored block with exact length
        out = gen_stored_of_length(target_len)
    elif variant == 1:
        # Single raw deflate compressed text
        text = rnd.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        reps = max(1, target_len // max(1, len(text)))
        data = (text * reps)[:target_len]
        out = gen_text_block(data, level=rnd.choice([1, 3, 6, 9]), strategy=rnd.choice([zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib.Z_FILTERED]))
    elif variant == 2:
        # Highly compressible run
        ch = rnd.choice([0x00, 0x20, 0x41, 0x61, 0xFF])
        data = gen_backref_runs(ch, target_len)
        out = deflate_raw(data, level=rnd.choice([1, 6, 9]))
    elif variant == 3:
        # Mixed payload, dynamic huffman likely
        data = gen_mixed_payload(rnd, target_len)
        out = deflate_raw(data, level=rnd.choice([1, 4, 6]), strategy=rnd.choice([zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib.Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY]))
    elif variant == 4:
        # Concatenated raw streams (multiple blocks)
        chunks = []
        remaining = target_len
        while remaining > 0:
            chunk_len = min(remaining, rnd.randint(1, min(64, remaining)))
            src = rnd.choice(ASCII_WORDS + BINARY_PATTERNS)
            if len(src) < chunk_len:
                reps = (chunk_len + len(src) - 1) // len(src)
                payload = (src * reps)[:chunk_len]
            else:
                start = rnd.randint(0, len(src) - chunk_len)
                payload = src[start:start + chunk_len]
            chunks.append(payload)
            remaining -= chunk_len
        out = make_concatenated_blocks(chunks)
    elif variant == 5:
        # Start with a stored block followed by a small compressed block
        part1 = bytes([rnd.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(min(target_len, rnd.randint(1, max(1, target_len//2))))])
        part2_len = max(0, target_len - len(part1))
        part2 = gen_backref_runs(rnd.choice([0x41, 0x00, 0xFF]), part2_len)
        stream1 = deflate_raw_stored_block(part1, final=False)
        stream2 = deflate_raw(part2, level=3)
        out = stream1 + stream2
    elif variant == 6:
        # Binary pattern compression
        src = rnd.choice(BINARY_PATTERNS)
        reps = max(1, target_len // max(1, len(src)))
        data = (src * reps)[:target_len]
        out = deflate_raw(data, level=rnd.choice([1, 6, 9]), strategy=rnd.choice([zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib.Z_RLE]))
    else:
        # Short literal sequence likely to use fixed trees
        data = bytes([rnd.randint(32, 126) for _ in range(target_len)])
        out = deflate_raw(data, level=1, strategy=zlib.Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY)

    # Ensure within 256 bytes for the stub; if too large (e.g., stored long), clamp.
    return clamp256(out)

import io
import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid ZIP archives tailored to the parser behavior
# described in the target. It focuses on classic (non-ZIP64) single-disk archives
# with a small number of entries, using only supported methods: store (0) and deflate (8).
# It avoids forbidden flags and creates consistent LFH/CDH/EOCDR with correct sizes,
# offsets, CRC32s, and optional data descriptor usage for deflate entries.
# The resulting buffer is <= 4096 bytes.

# Constants (ZIP structures / signatures)
S_LFH = 0x04034B50
S_CDH = 0x02014B50
S_EOCDR = 0x06054B50
S_DDR = 0x08074B50  # optional signature for data descriptor

# DOS time/date helpers
# MS-DOS date: Y from 1980, bits: Y(7) M(4) D(5)
# MS-DOS time: H(5) M(6) S/2(5)

def dos_time_date(seed: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    year = r.randrange(1980, 2099 + 1)
    month = r.randrange(1, 12 + 1)
    day = r.randrange(1, 28 + 1)  # stay in safe range
    hour = r.randrange(0, 23 + 1)
    minute = r.randrange(0, 59 + 1)
    second = r.randrange(0, 29 + 1) * 2  # even seconds
    dos_date = ((year - 1980) << 9) | (month << 5) | day
    dos_time = (hour << 11) | (minute << 5) | (second // 2)
    return dos_time, dos_date


def safe_name_components(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Generate safe path components: no control chars, no '..', no backslashes, no empty
    alpha = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
    comps = []
    depth = r.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 3])  # prefer shorter
    for i in range(depth):
        base = ''.join(r.choice(alpha) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
        comps.append(base)
    # Optional trailing slash only for directories (we won't generate directory entries here)
    return comps


def make_filename(r: random.Random, directory: bool = False, ext: str = '') -> str:
    comps = safe_name_components(r)
    leaf = comps[-1]
    if ext and not directory:
        leaf = leaf + ext
    comps[-1] = leaf
    name = '/'.join(comps)
    if directory and not name.endswith('/'):
        name += '/'
    return name


def deflate_raw(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Raw DEFLATE stream (no zlib header). Python exposes wbits=-15 via zlib.compressobj
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level=6, wbits=-15)
    out = comp.compress(data) + comp.flush()
    return out


def crc32_u32(data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


class Entry:
    def __init__(self,
                 name: str,
                 method: int,
                 data: bytes,
                 use_ddr: bool):
        self.name = name.encode('utf-8')  # We will not set UTF-8 flag; ensure no NUL
        self.method = method
        self.use_ddr = use_ddr
        self.uncompressed = data
        if method == 0:
            self.compressed = data
        elif method == 8:
            self.compressed = deflate_raw(data)
        else:
            raise ValueError('unsupported method')
        self.crc32 = crc32_u32(self.uncompressed)
        self.time, self.date = dos_time_date(crc32_u32(self.name) ^ len(self.uncompressed))
        # Filled later:
        self.lfh_offset = 0
        self.lfh_length = 0
        self.data_offset = 0
        self.ddr = b''

    def build_lfh(self) -> bytes:
        # General purpose bit flag: bit 3 indicates data descriptor when use_ddr.
        flags = 0x0008 if self.use_ddr else 0x0000
        version_needed = 20  # 2.0
        extra = b''  # keep empty for simplicity
        fn = self.name
        # If DDR is used, LFH must have crc32 and sizes set to 0 per spec and matcher
        crc = 0 if self.use_ddr else self.crc32
        csize = 0 if self.use_ddr else len(self.compressed)
        usize = 0 if self.use_ddr else len(self.uncompressed)
        lfh = struct.pack('<IHHHHHIIIHH',
                          S_LFH,
                          version_needed,
                          flags,
                          self.method,
                          self.time,
                          self.date,
                          crc,
                          csize,
                          usize,
                          len(fn),
                          len(extra))
        self.lfh_length = len(lfh) + len(fn) + len(extra)
        return lfh + fn + extra

    def build_ddr(self) -> bytes:
        if not self.use_ddr:
            self.ddr = b''
            return b''
        # Emit data descriptor with signature (commonly accepted), 32-bit sizes
        self.ddr = struct.pack('<IIII', S_DDR, self.crc32,
                               len(self.compressed), len(self.uncompressed))
        return self.ddr

    def build_cdh(self) -> bytes:
        # Version made by: set to Unix (3<<8) + 20
        version_made_by = (3 << 8) | 20
        version_needed = 20
        flags = 0x0008 if self.use_ddr else 0x0000
        comp_method = self.method
        crc = self.crc32
        csize = len(self.compressed)
        usize = len(self.uncompressed)
        fn = self.name
        extra = b''
        comment = b''
        disk = 0
        internal = 0
        # External attributes; ensure regular file perms without special bits
        external = (0o100644 & 0xFFFF) << 16
        relative_offset = self.lfh_offset
        cdh_fixed = struct.pack('<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',
                                S_CDH,
                                version_made_by,
                                version_needed,
                                flags,
                                comp_method,
                                self.time,
                                self.date,
                                crc,
                                csize,
                                usize,
                                len(fn),
                                len(extra),
                                len(comment),
                                disk,
                                internal,
                                external,
                                relative_offset)
        return cdh_fixed + fn + extra + comment


def build_zip(entries: List[Entry]) -> bytes:
    out = io.BytesIO()
    # Write LFHs + data (+ optional DDR) sequentially
    for e in entries:
        e.lfh_offset = out.tell()
        lfh = e.build_lfh()
        out.write(lfh)
        e.data_offset = out.tell()
        out.write(e.compressed)
        out.write(e.build_ddr())
    cd_start = out.tell()
    # Central directory
    for e in entries:
        out.write(e.build_cdh())
    cd_end = out.tell()
    cd_size = cd_end - cd_start
    # EOCDR
    total_entries = len(entries)
    disk = 0
    cd_disk = 0
    cd_records_disk = total_entries
    cd_records_total = total_entries
    comment = b''
    eocdr = struct.pack('<IHHHHIIH',
                        S_EOCDR,
                        disk,
                        cd_disk,
                        cd_records_disk,
                        cd_records_total,
                        cd_size,
                        cd_start,
                        len(comment))
    out.write(eocdr)
    out.write(comment)
    return out.getvalue()


def random_payload(r: random.Random, typ: str) -> bytes:
    if typ == 'text':
        words = [b'lorem', b'ipsum', b'dolor', b'sit', b'amet', b'zip', b'pure', b'data']
        n = r.randint(10, 80)
        sep = b' '
        payload = sep.join(r.choice(words) for _ in range(n)) + b"\n"
        return payload
    elif typ == 'binary':
        size = r.randint(16, 256)
        # Structured binary: repeating pattern to compress well sometimes
        block = bytes((i % 251 for i in range(r.randint(8, 32))))
        payload = (block * (size // len(block) + 1))[:size]
        return payload
    elif typ == 'smallzero':
        return b''  # Will handle empty via specific deflate empty stream or stored empty
    else:
        size = r.randint(1, 128)
        return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))


def make_entries(seed: int, r: random.Random) -> List[Entry]:
    entries: List[Entry] = []
    count = r.choice([1, 1, 2, 3])
    for i in range(count):
        # Alternate between stored and deflated entries
        method = r.choice([0, 8])
        # Choose payload type to vary compression behavior
        ptype = r.choice(['text', 'binary', 'random'])
        data = random_payload(r, ptype)
        # Ensure no zero-sized uncompressed for deflate except allow 2-byte empty stream case.
        if method == 8 and len(data) == 0:
            data = b'A' * r.randint(1, 32)
        # Data descriptor only for deflate entries sometimes
        use_ddr = (method == 8) and r.choice([True, False])
        name_ext = '.txt' if ptype == 'text' else ('.bin' if ptype == 'binary' else '')
        name = make_filename(r, directory=False, ext=name_ext)
        # Ensure name has no NUL and only forward slashes already guaranteed
        e = Entry(name=name, method=method, data=data, use_ddr=use_ddr)
        entries.append(e)
    # Keep total size under limit by trimming to first N entries if needed later
    return entries


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Build between 1 and 3 entries and ensure final size <= 4096; if exceeded, reduce entries
    for _ in range(5):
        entries = make_entries(seed ^ r.getrandbits(32), r)
        buf = build_zip(entries)
        if len(buf) <= 4096:
            return buf
        # Try with fewer entries
        if len(entries) > 1:
            buf = build_zip(entries[:1])
            if len(buf) <= 4096:
                return buf
    # Fallback: single tiny stored file
    tiny = Entry(name='a/b/c.txt', method=0, data=b'hi\n', use_ddr=False)
    return build_zip([tiny])
